name: Asylum / Refugee Status Determination

qualifying_event.description: Fiji is one of six Pacific signatories to the 1951 Refugee Convention. There is no standalone Refugee Act -- asylum/refugee status is administered through the general Immigration Act 2003 permit framework plus a joint UNHCR-Fiji Immigration Department Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on refugee status determination, meaning Fiji runs its own domestic RSD process rather than pure UNHCR-mandate processing, but on a thin and evolving legal footing. Fiji's own Immigration Department has publicly acknowledged (Sept 2026) that it lacks clearer legal and procedural frameworks, describing contested status determinations leading to legal challenges.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence of a well-founded fear of persecution on Convention grounds.

requirements.blocker_text: Well-founded fear of persecution on Convention grounds, assessed under the joint UNHCR-Fiji Immigration Department SOP.

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Fiji). STATUS: DRAFT -- the hard requirement is sourced to a tier-2 UNHCR briefing note rather than a tier-1 statute, since Fiji has no standalone Refugee Act; the tier-1 immigration.gov.fj page confirms the category exists but discloses no procedural detail. STRUCTURAL FINDING: Fiji sits in an unusual middle position in this dataset -- it runs a genuinely DOMESTIC refugee-status-determination process (not pure UNHCR-mandate processing as seen in Jordan/Mongolia/Cote d'Ivoire elsewhere in this dataset), but on a thin, contested legal footing that Fiji's own immigration officials have publicly admitted (as of September 2026 reporting) needs reform -- disputed status determinations have led to legal challenges. Caseload is tiny: approximately 38 individuals granted refugee status 2018-2025 (8 years), per press reporting (tier 3/4, not independently corroborated at tier 1/2, so not restated in outcome fields as a stable figure). Appeal mechanism/timeframe and the specific permit type issued to recognized refugees were not confirmed at any tier. CONFIRMED NOT A ROUTE, per explicit research: Fiji has no legal climate-migration/displacement pathway for other Pacific nations -- the well-known 2014 Kiribati government land purchase on Vanua Levu was a private land acquisition, not a bilateral migration treaty, and confers no immigration status on Kiribati citizens. Also confirmed not a Fiji inbound route: PACER Plus labour mobility and the Pacific Labour/RSE/PALM schemes move Fijian workers OUT to Australia/New Zealand -- Fiji is the sending country, not the destination, so these are not modeled here.
